context: seed: an exported CSV of this world ends with a TOTAL row that is not a record (suite/families/curriculum.py:192); every clothing of the footer-row lesson sums the amount column or counts the records under a budget of one or two shell calls
counterfactual: The overshoot is aggregating every row after the header — the naive policies at suite/families/curriculum.py:198 and suite/families/curriculum.py:203 — when the export is built with a TOTAL row at suite/families/curriculum.py:192, so the naive sum is twice the gold and the naive count one over.
decision: An exported CSV (a `*-export.csv`, columns such as ref,account,amount) ends with a trailer row whose first field is `TOTAL` and which is not a record. Before summing a column or counting records, drop the header and every row whose first field is TOTAL, in one shell call: `awk -F, 'NR>1 && $1!="TOTAL" {t+=$3} END{print t+0}' <file>` for a sum of the third column, `awk -F, 'NR>1 && $1!="TOTAL"' <file> | wc -l` for a record count. Never inspect the file first. A sum that includes the trailer is exactly double the answer; a count that includes it is one too many.

residue: whether a row that is not marked TOTAL is still a summary row is judgment

not_this: a CSV with a name or customer column that may be quoted — that is the quoted-field rule, and both apply when one file has both
a line total over plain files
